tagline: Poland's former royal capital has one of Europe's largest medieval market squares, Wawel Castle above the Vistula and the historic Jewish quarter of Kazimierz.
overview: Kraków was Poland's capital for more than 500 years, and unlike Warsaw its old town survived World War II largely intact. The historic centre was among the first places listed by UNESCO in 1978, and Rynek Główny, its 13th-century main square, is one of the largest medieval squares in Europe.

The square is framed by the Cloth Hall, a Renaissance market hall, and St Mary's Basilica, where a trumpeter plays the hejnał from the tower every hour and stops mid-tune. The Royal Road leads south to Wawel Hill, with the royal castle and the cathedral where most Polish kings were crowned and buried.

Kazimierz, the old Jewish quarter, is now full of synagogues, cafés and bars, and across the river Oskar Schindler's factory is a museum on the wartime occupation. Day trips go to the Wieliczka Salt Mine and to the Auschwitz-Birkenau memorial.

funFacts.title: CAPITAL FOR 500 YEARS
funFacts.text: Kraków was Poland's capital until the royal court moved to Warsaw around 1596.

funFacts.title: A GIANT MEDIEVAL SQUARE
funFacts.text: Rynek Główny covers about 4 hectares, one of Europe's largest medieval squares.

funFacts.title: THE BROKEN TUNE
funFacts.text: The hourly trumpet call from St Mary's stops abruptly, recalling a legendary guard shot mid-call.

funFacts.title: AMONG UNESCO'S FIRST
funFacts.text: Kraków's historic centre was on UNESCO's first World Heritage list in 1978.

funFacts.title: KINGS IN THE CATHEDRAL
funFacts.text: Most Polish monarchs were crowned and buried in Wawel Cathedral.

funFacts.title: A DRAGON ON THE HILL
funFacts.text: Legend says the Wawel Dragon lived in a cave below the castle; a statue there breathes fire.

funFacts.title: A SALT CATHEDRAL
funFacts.text: The Wieliczka mine's Chapel of St Kinga is carved entirely from rock salt.

funFacts.title: AN ANCIENT UNIVERSITY
funFacts.text: Jagiellonian University, founded in 1364, is one of Europe's oldest; Copernicus studied there.

funFacts.title: OBWARZANEK
funFacts.text: Ring-shaped obwarzanek bread rolls are sold from carts all over town.

funFacts.title: SPARED BY WAR
funFacts.text: Kraków's old town came through World War II with little damage.
